status: Reported selected counts and joins independently reproduced; interpretive limits retained
method: Read source CSV/pipe-delimited files independently using bundled Python; constructed unique eligible contract-plan-segment-formulary tuples; used explicit RxCUI sets for oral estradiol, vaginal cream, Veozah and Intrarosa; independently selected generic estradiol patch concepts from the CMS reference; joined formulary membership directly to plan tuples. Did not import or execute analyze_formularies.py. Queried every unmatched RxCUI using NIH RxNav historystatus API.
interpretive_review: No arithmetic or join defect identified. Only the listed selected product counts were independently recomputed; remaining groups were inspected in code and target definitions, not separately recalculated.
CMS defines a plan using contract, plan and segment. Retain plan-segment language and distinguish 5,055 contract-plan pairs from 5,499 segments.
Scope excludes non-Part-D, employer, PACE and demonstration plans except included MMPs; 19 suppressed plan-segments are excluded.
Presence means at least one matching listed strength/product. It does not mean every formulation, every strength, every manufacturer or every indication is covered.
PA_N is a field observation. It does not establish absence of quantity limits, diagnosis restrictions, age edits, pharmacy requirements or denied claims. The basic-file NDC is a proxy NDC.
The calculation named without_PA_or_ST actually requires PA_N and ST_N on the same listed option; describe it as neither PA nor ST.
Drug groups have different indications, routes, alternatives, prices and safety considerations. Comparisons do not independently establish sex or gender discrimination.
The monthly data are plan-segment-weighted rather than enrollment-weighted, and are an August 2026 snapshot, not September claims data.
All 23 unmatched identifiers were resolved and none maps to estradiol, testosterone, fezolinetant, ospemifene or prasterone. Their absence from the CMS reference does not affect target counts.

Viagra aggregate claims lack indication and benefit basis. Do not assert they are ED claims, pulmonary-hypertension claims, supplemental payments, federal reimbursement or improper payments. Current retrieved public methodology did not resolve supplemental-only inclusion.
Gross annual drug spending includes plan and beneficiary amounts before rebates. Estradiol* aggregates routes; it is not all estradiol products and is not a female-only beneficiary count.
